notes.content:
**Executive summary:** The INC (1885) began an **organised political movement**. From 1885 to 1916 it passed through:
1. **Moderate phase (1885–1905)** — prayer, petition, protest.
2. **Radical phase (from 1905)** — Partition of Bengal, Swadeshi, Boycott, revolutionaries, **Surat Split (1907)**.
3. **Unity (1916)** — **Lucknow Pact** and **Home Rule League**.

Meanwhile the British tried to **divide Hindus and Muslims** — Partition of Bengal, Muslim League (1906), **separate electorates** (1909).

fiveW.who: Dadabhai Naoroji, Surendranath Banerjee, Pherozeshah Mehta, Gopal Krishna Gokhale
fiveW.where: Indian National Congress sessions; delegations to England
fiveW.why: Believed British rule was benevolent and could be persuaded
fiveW.how: Prayer, petition, protest — resolutions, pamphlets, lectures, newspapers, delegations

notes.content:
**Beliefs:** British rule was **benevolent**; Indians **not yet ready** to govern themselves; the British could be **persuaded** to reform.

**Leaders:** educated middle class — teachers, lawyers, journalists, industrialists — **Dadabhai Naoroji, Surendranath Banerjee, Pherozeshah Mehta, Gopal Krishna Gokhale**.

**Method — 'Prayer, Petition, Protest' (3 P's):** no violence; faith in **British fair play**; resolutions and petitions; pamphlets, lectures, articles; processions; **delegations to England**.

**Demands**
• **Reduce high taxes**.
• **ICS exams simultaneously in India and England**.
• **Indians in high posts**.
• **Reduce military expenditure**.
• Change British **economic policies** to benefit Indians.

notes.subtopic: 3. Achievements and Failures of the Moderates
notes.content:
**Criticism:** achieved few objectives; called a **'microscopic minority'** — represented only a small section; masses untouched.

**Achievements**
• Spread **national consciousness** — people felt they belonged to **one nation**.
• Made Indians aware of **freedom, secularism and democracy**.
• Supported **social reform** — against rigid caste.
• (Topper extra: Dadabhai Naoroji's **Drain Theory** exposed economic exploitation.)

fiveW.who: Lala Lajpat Rai (Punjab), Bal Gangadhar Tilak (Maharashtra), Bipin Chandra Pal (Bengal)
fiveW.why: Moderate methods had failed; no faith in British justice
fiveW.how: Mass agitation, Swadeshi, Boycott; sacrifice, even violence if needed

notes.content:
**Leaders — 'Lal-Bal-Pal':** **Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal**.

**Beliefs**
• **No faith** in British justice and fair play.
• British rule did **more harm than good**.
• Demanded **complete independence (Swaraj)** — not self-government within the Empire. (Tilak: *'Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it.'*)

**Method:** **aggressive, organised mass agitation**; ready for sacrifice, even violence.

**Achievements:** promoted **Indian-made goods** to revive industry; **broadened the social base** by involving the **masses**.

| | Moderates | Radicals |
|---|---|---|
| Faith in British | Yes | No |
| Goal | Reforms, self-government within Empire | **Swaraj** |
| Method | Prayer, petition, protest | Mass agitation, Swadeshi, Boycott |
| Base | Educated few | **Masses** |

fiveW.where: Bengal → East Bengal and West Bengal
fiveW.why: Official: too large to administer. Real: divide Hindus and Muslims and weaken nationalism
fiveW.how: Formal partition; opposed by the Swadeshi and Boycott movements

notes.content:
• **Official reason:** Bengal too large for efficient administration; to develop neglected **eastern Bengal** (Dhaka) — Curzon laid the foundation of **Curzon Hall**, Dhaka (1904).
• **Real reason:** **'divide and rule'** — drive a wedge between **Hindus and Muslims** and weaken the national movement.
• **16 October 1905** — Bengal partitioned into **East Bengal and West Bengal**.
• **1911** — Bengal **reunited**; **capital moved from Calcutta to Delhi**.

**Now:** Dhaka is the capital of **Bangladesh**; Curzon Hall is part of the University of Dhaka.

notes.subtopic: 6. Swadeshi, Boycott, Revolutionaries and the Surat Split

fiveW.who: Radical nationalists and young revolutionaries (Khudiram Bose, Barin Ghosh, Hemchandra Kanungo)
fiveW.what: Swadeshi and Boycott movements; revolutionary activity; split in the Congress
fiveW.why: Protest against the Partition of Bengal and British injustice
fiveW.how: Using Indian goods, boycotting British goods and schools; secret societies, bombs

notes.content:
**Swadeshi** — use only **Indian-made goods**.
**Boycott** — refuse **British/foreign goods** and **British schools and colleges**.

**Revolutionaries**
• Formed **underground (secret) societies** — centres: **Bengal, Maharashtra, UP, Punjab**.
• Published anti-British papers, collected arms, **made bombs**, attacked officials.
• Harsh repression: **Khudiram Bose hanged**; **Barin Ghosh, Hemchandra Kanungo** imprisoned in the **Andaman and Nicobar Islands**.

**Surat Split (1907):** differences between moderates and radicals split the Congress at the **Surat session**; radicals left the Congress.

**Comparative history:** **Russo-Japanese War (1904–05)** — Japan became the **first Asian power to defeat a European power** — inspired Indians.

fiveW.who: Muslim deputation to Lord Minto; Nawab Salimullah of Dacca; Lord Minto and John Morley
fiveW.what: All India Muslim League; Indian Council Act with separate electorates
fiveW.why: Muslims sought separate representation; the British wanted to divide Hindus and Muslims
fiveW.how: League founded at a meeting in Dacca; the 1909 Act created separate electorates

notes.content:
**All India Muslim League (1906)**
• A Muslim deputation met **Lord Minto** asking for **separate representation**; Minto agreed.
• Founded at **Dacca** on the initiative of **Nawab Salimullah**.
• **Welcomed by the British** — separate parties would keep communities apart.
• **Aims:** loyalty to the British; protect Muslims' **political rights**; platform for **upper-class Muslims**.
• **Mohammed Ali Jinnah** joined in **1913**; later first **Governor-General of Pakistan** ('Quaid-e-Azam').

**Indian Council Act 1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms)** — Viceroy **Minto**, Secretary of State **John Morley**.
• **Separate electorates** — Muslims vote only for Muslims, Hindus for Hindus → **kept communities divided**.

notes.subtopic: 8. Lucknow Pact and Home Rule League (1916)

fiveW.who: Congress and Muslim League; Annie Besant and Bal Gangadhar Tilak
fiveW.why: League shifted to self-government (angered by British stand on the Ottoman caliph); need for unity
fiveW.how: Joint session at Lucknow; Home Rule Leagues roused the masses for Swaraj

notes.content:
**Change in the League:** in **1916** it demanded **self-government** within the Empire — Muslims were upset at British support for ending the **Ottoman Empire** (its sultan was the **caliph**).

**Lucknow Pact (1916)** — joint session of **Congress and Muslim League** at Lucknow.
• **Hindus and Muslims united** again after the Partition of Bengal.
• **Radicals returned** to the Congress → stronger movement.

**Home Rule League (1916)** — **Annie Besant and Bal Gangadhar Tilak**.
• Demanded **Swaraj / self-government**.
• **Aroused the masses**, revived the **Swadeshi** spirit, forced some administrative changes.

questions.question: Who partitioned Bengal? What was the motive? What did the radicals do?
questions.answer:
• Lord Curzon, 16 October 1905.
  • Motive: officially better administration; really to divide Hindus and Muslims and weaken the national movement.
  • Radicals launched Swadeshi and Boycott movements; some formed revolutionary secret societies.

questions.question: What was the Boycott Movement?
questions.answer: Launched after the Partition of Bengal, it asked Indians to stop buying British or foreign goods and not to send their children to British schools and colleges. It went hand in hand with Swadeshi — using Indian-made goods.

questions.question: Name two revolutionaries imprisoned in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
questions.answer: Barin Ghosh and Hemchandra Kanungo. (Khudiram Bose was hanged.)

questions.question: How did the Surat Split affect the national movement?
questions.answer:
• At Surat (1907) the Congress split between moderates and radicals.
  • The movement was weakened; the British repressed the radicals separately and tried to win over the moderates (Morley-Minto Reforms).
  • Unity returned only with the Lucknow Pact (1916), when the radicals rejoined.

questions.question: What were separate electorates? Why did the British introduce them?
questions.answer:
• Under the Indian Council Act 1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms), voters were divided by religion — Muslims voted only for Muslims, Hindus only for Hindus.
  • The British used them to keep Hindus and Muslims divided ('divide and rule') and weaken the united national movement.

questions.question: Why did the British try to divide the country on the basis of religion?
questions.answer:
• A united national movement threatened British rule.
  • Dividing Hindus and Muslims (Partition of Bengal, welcoming the Muslim League, separate electorates) would stop them uniting against the British.
  • This policy of 'divide and rule' helped the British keep control.

questions.question: Why was the Lucknow Pact important?
questions.answer:
• Signed in 1916 at the joint session of the Congress and Muslim League at Lucknow.
  • Hindus and Muslims were united again after the Partition of Bengal.
  • The radicals rejoined the Congress, strengthening the movement.

questions.question: Who founded the Home Rule League? Explain its role.
questions.answer:
• Founded in 1916 by Annie Besant and Bal Gangadhar Tilak.
  • Demanded Swaraj / self-government.
  • Aroused the masses, revived the Swadeshi spirit and forced the British to make some administrative changes.
